item: Frozen 60-second Mandarin clip with its reference transcript
why: L2-2 to L2-6. Decided by 念誠 on 2026-10-28 (eval/README.md section 8): a CC0 public Chinese recording, with transcript and source. Not fetched here. build_clip.py turns the chosen source into clip/clip.wav (16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM, exactly 60.000 s; about 1.9 MB, over the 1 MB aim because WAV is the one input every speech CLI reads), clip/warmup.wav (first 10 s), clip/reference.txt and clip/SOURCE.json. The reference must contain at least 60 script-differing characters and about 55 s of speech, so that 50 s of cue coverage is reachable. Clips are chosen by a rule fixed before anyone listens to or transcribes them (calibration.md), never by trying a tool on them.

candidates.source: Mozilla Common Voice, Chinese (Taiwan) zh-TW subset, validated clips: https://commonvoice.mozilla.org/zh-TW/datasets (dataset downloads may now be served through the Mozilla Data Collective; use whichever the site points to on the download date)
candidates.license: CC0-1.0 (dataset); the download page asks users not to try to identify speakers
candidates.size: only about 12-15 clips of about 5 s are kept (tens of KB each as MP3); the downloaded archive is much larger
candidates.pin: corpus version name + each kept clip's file name + SHA-256 of each MP3 + its sentence text from validated.tsv, all in SOURCE.json via build_clip.py concat; Traditional-script sentences, Taiwanese Mandarin speakers

candidates.source: Mozilla Common Voice, Chinese (China) zh-CN subset, validated clips: https://commonvoice.mozilla.org/zh-CN/datasets
candidates.pin: as above; the sentences are in Simplified script, so reference stats are computed after OpenCC s2tw (zh_score.py ref-stats does this); mainland accents

candidates.source: LibriVox: one solo Mandarin reading of a public-domain modern vernacular text (catalogue at https://librivox.org/ filtered by language Chinese; the files are on archive.org)
candidates.license: LibriVox dedicates its recordings to the public domain; confirm the item's archive.org record states CC0 or the Creative Commons public-domain dedication before using it, since 念誠's decision says CC0
candidates.size: one chapter MP3 (tens of MB) of which a 60 s window is kept
candidates.pin: archive.org identifier + file name + SHA-256 + start offset, via build_clip.py cut; reference = the published text of that passage, corrected by ear to what is actually read

item: Pinned OpenCC (the shared OpenCC scorer, also used by q11)
why: L2-3 converts reference and output to Traditional; L2-4 is the shared scorer of eval/README.md section 5. Both use eval/fixtures/_shared/zh_script.py with one pinned set of OpenCC dictionary files, listed once in eval/fixtures/_shared/needs.json (no OpenCC package).
L2-2: 'parses with the pinned SRT parser'. srt_check.py uses the srt package's parse() and adds the sequence, timing and coverage checks itself.

candidates.pin: srt==X.Y.Z (3.5.3 was current when last known; confirm) + wheel SHA-256
version + SHA-256 (srt_check.py would need a small adapter)

item: openai-whisper 'small' baseline for the speed item
why: L2-5 compares against openai-whisper 'small' with default settings, in its own container. baseline/run_baseline.sh installs and runs it; it refuses to run until every pin is set.

candidates.pin: WHISPER_VERSION = latest release on the pin date

candidates.source: https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu (torch CPU wheel for cp312 manylinux x86_64)
candidates.pin: TORCH_VERSION + TORCH_INDEX_URL; record pip freeze from the setup run

candidates.source: the 'small' checkpoint URL listed in openai-whisper's source (_MODELS in whisper/__init__.py); the path contains the file's SHA-256
candidates.pin: SMALL_PT_SHA256 (run_baseline.sh checks it after the warm-up download)

candidates.source: Ubuntu 24.04 package ffmpeg (needed by openai-whisper to read audio)
candidates.pin: package version from apt-cache policy on the pin date
